system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

data.summary: The alert tells the public to disregard an earlier weather alert as sent in error and says no action is needed. No input supports this. The only verified hazard input is an active NCM fog warning for western regions, 21:30 on 17 Feb to 10:00 on 18 Feb, with visibility possibly dropping to zero. A retraction would contradict the bulletin. Whether any earlier alert was truly erroneous, and whether a separate correct fog warning must go out, is for the issuing authority to decide.

objections.issue: The description says an earlier alert was sent in error. No event input reports such an error. The verified NCM bulletin confirms a live fog hazard over this period, so the alert contradicts the bulletin and rests on an unverified claim.
objections.fix: A person at the issuing authority must confirm whether an earlier alert was actually erroneous. If it was a genuine fog alert, do not retract it. Issue or keep a fog warning matching NCM: fog and reduced visibility, possibly zero, across several western regions, from 21:30 on 17 Feb until 10:00 on 18 Feb. If a true cancellation is needed, it must reference the specific erroneous message as a Cancel and must not imply the NCM fog hazard is void.

objections.issue: The instruction 'No action is needed' contradicts NCM's advice to motorists during the warning period. It understates the hazard, and it is inconsistent with the alert's own severity Moderate and certainty Likely for a fog warning.
objections.fix: Unless the authority confirms there is no fog hazard, replace this with NCM's advice. Drivers should exercise extreme caution, keep a safe distance, and follow the modified speed limits in thick fog.
